text:
maya: dropping a fresh mock for the capacity panel. main questions: slider vs numeric inputs for min/max, how the SLO slider should snap, and what guardrails to show inline. figma: https://www.figma.com/file/NEW/capacity-panel liam: nice. first impression: summary cards at top are helpful. nit: min/max numeric inputs and slider positions need to stay in sync when someone types a number. sara: agree. prefer primary UX to be keyboard-first: allow tabbing into min, type number, press Enter to apply to slider. mobile still uses slider by default. ethan: accessibility: when numbers update the SLO estimate, announce via aria-live="polite". also make the SLO slider have tick marks and visible values for screen reader users. olivia: product callout: the SLO slider should have snap points that map to precomputed profiles (e.g., "low-latency", "balanced", "cost-optimized"). each snap should show a short tooltip explaining tradeoffs. maya: added snap labels in figma. question: should snap points lock min/max suggestions or just prefill recommended values? liam: recommendation: snapping should propose values but keep them editable. show a small badge "recommended" and a one-click apply. avoids surprising users. sara: microcopy: change 'SLO slider' -> 'Latency target' label and add helper text 'Adjust the 99th percentile latency you want to aim for.' keeps language user-focused.en: burst UX: when burst is turned on, show an inline max-peak estimate and a short cooldown description. if min==max, disable burst toggle and show tooltip "burst needs headroom". kelsey: mobile constraint: make numeric fields compact with clear affordance for increment/decrement and make sure touch targets >= 44px. ethan: keyboard flow: sample aria snippet in comments: ```html
Expected 99p latency: 120ms (estimate)
``` liam: UI polish: animate slider handle only subtly when numbers change. big jumps feel jarring. also show unit suffixes on numbers ($/mo, ms, GPUs). olivia: guardrails: propose three states: info (ok), warning (SLO degraded by X%), and hard-block (violates hard guardrail). display them inline under the summary row, not as a blocking modal unless it's hard-block. sara: copy for warning state: "This change may increase 99p latency by ~15% — consider raising max or enabling burst." for hard-block: "This change violates your configured SLO guardrail and cannot be applied." maya: good. we should add an undo window after apply (e.g., "Undo changes" toast for 2 minutes) in case teams misconfigure during peak traffic.en: backend note: when applying, capture snapshot of assumptions used for estimates and attach to rollout event so we can audit later. ethan: perf/UI: debounce estimate calls 300ms on slider drag, but fire immediately on numeric input confirm. show skeleton on cards while computing. liam: QA scenarios: rapid slider scrubbing, switching pools mid-edit, min greater than max guard, enabling burst with insufficient pool capacity. kelsey: accessibility checklist: labels for increment/decrement buttons, aria-live for status messages, focusable recommended presets, contrast for tick marks. olivia: suggestion: add an "expert mode" toggle to reveal advanced knobs (burst cooldown, prewarm count) for platform teams; hide for standard users. sara: copy tweak: change CTA from "Save" to "Apply capacity changes" and secondary "Preview in console" for visual confirmation before provisioning. maya: design decision: show top summary row with three compact cards: cost delta, latency delta, pool. clicking any opens detail accordion below. ben: pool selection UX: chips with pool name, free GPUs, and a small icon if pool supports burst. selecting a pool updates estimates live. liam: small iconography note: make sure icons have text alternatives for screen readers and that color isn't the only signal for pool state. maya: action items: - implement numeric+slider sync (liam) - SLO snap presets + recommended badge (olivia) - guardrail visuals & copy (sara) - debounce + skeleton + aria-live (ethan) - pool chips + burst badge + mobile chips (ben + kelsey) - undo toast spec (maya) deploy-bot: uploaded image -> capacity-panel-v4.png maya: thanks all. aiming to freeze copy by Friday and ship a staging prototype early next week. ping in thread with any follow-ups. :thumbsup:
